verdict.label: Worth checking
verdict.headline: Rey Cortiço Lunch
verdict.reason: Rey Cortiço is worth a quick check for lunch, but it is not a guaranteed session.  Treat it as a check-first call rather than a sure thing.  Wind is the main thing to watch.  The tide should let the sandbars work without overdoing it.

conversationalSummary.text: Today I’d treat Rey Cortiço around lunch as the best option, but do a proper Surfline + MEO Beachcam check before you leave—wind angle looks off and Surfline consistency isn’t great. The tide is mid rising, so you might get a rare bit of shape/punch from the sandbanks, but the risk of it being messy from cross-onshore wind is real. If the cams don’t look noticeably better than expected, I’d skip it and save the drive.

best.explanation: Rey Cortiço looks like a small north coast window for Rare window, Medium confidence: 0.3-0.6 m, 53 kJ, 8 s period, lully 23/100, and wind is the main risk.  An open beach break where the sandbanks decide everything; this is best for quiet, punchy peaks when Lagide is too small; 6-9s at mid tide can turn Belgas punchy and rippable, so checking exposed beaches makes sense.  Watch: Surfline consistency is lully; wind angle is poor for this spot.

Watch: wind angle is poor for this spot; Meio da Baia may feel too soft without more push.
